Board category: All-Mountain / All-Mountain Freestyle [1][5] 6. Gender: Men's [1][108] 7. First year DOA model was available for sale: 2012/2013 season (introduced the year prior, "first time last year" per Whitelines 2013 review) [88] 8. DOA has been a best-seller since approximately 2012: "it's been a best selling board on the Capita lineup since 2012" [35] 9. Manufacturer: CAPiTA Snowboards (operated by C3 Worldwide LLC, Seattle WA; parent Core S.r.l., Delebio, Italy) [22] 10. Founded: Seattle, 2000 [44] 11. Manufacturing location: The Mothership, Feistritz, Carinthia region, southern Austria [6][42][45] 12. Factory: 52,000 sq ft facility, opened November 2015 [48] 13. Clean energy: 100% clean energy manufacturing using on-site hydro-activated NH3 Thermal Energy System and solar panels [22][42] 14. Sustainability: Zero CO2 emissions, zero ozone depletion potential, zero global warming potential in production [22][48] 15. Certified B Corporation with B Impact Score of 98.9 (median for ordinary businesses: 50.9) [44] 16. FSC certified wood cores used [43] 17. Supply chain: 98% raw materials sourced locally (50% Austria, 16% Germany, 15% Slovenia, 14% Switzerland, 3% Italy, 2% Asia) [46] 18. NFC chip: Embedded in the nose of the board for registration, warranty, and production tracking (since 2020) [22][51] 19. Factory edge bevel: 1 degree [95] 20. Factory wax: Factory waxed for most normal winter conditions [95] SHAPE & GEOMETRY 21. Shape: True Twin (symmetrical, identical tip and tail) [1][22] 22. Taper: 0 (zero taper, confirming true twin) [Manufacturer site] 23. Stance setback: Centered [19][66] 24. Flex direction: Twin flex (symmetrical) [Manufacturer site] 25. Camber type: Resort V1 + Flat Kick Tech [1][22] 26. Camber description: Traditional camber between the feet, transitioning to flat (zero camber), then reverse camber at the tip/tail, with Flat Kick technology [1][22][89] 27. Sidecut type: Blended Radial [1][22] 28. Sidecut description: Single-radius arc through midsection with custom blend zones at contact points [1][16] 29. Mounting pattern: 2x4 inserts [1][16] CONSTRUCTION 30. Core material: P2 Superlight Core — Paulownia and Poplar wood blend [1][16][22] 31. Core description: Extremely lightweight and versatile with high impact resistance and maximum pop [22][16] 32. Core upgrade history: P2 Superlight core introduced for 2023 season, replaced Dual Blaster V2 Core [52][64] 33. Laminate: Hybrid Carbon HolySheet Bi/Bi — bi-axial fiberglass above and below core with carbon interwoven into bottom layer [1][16][22] 34. HolySheet carbon interwoven update: New for 2025 model year [10][29] 35. Resin: Magic Bean Resin — plant-based, 60% bio-content from renewable agricultural raw material [1][53] 36. Resin properties: Zero waste, no greenhouse emissions, low production temperatures, enhanced rigidity allows thinner wood core [53] 37. Carbon reinforcement: Carbon Fiber Boosters [6][22] 38. Sidewall construction: Fortress Aramid (Kevlar) Bound Sidewalls — Kevlar "S" wrap from top of sidewall to underside of core [10][41] 39. Topsheet: PLT Technology — Digital and Screen Print with Metallic Underlay [1][22] 40. Topsheet method: Bonds topsheet to already-pressed board without fiberglass showing through; no lacquer needed [1][22] 41. Printing: PAM16000 — 16,000 inkjet nozzles, solventless water-based UV ink, plus hand screen printing [1][16] 42. Base material: Quantum Drive Base — sintered ultra-high-molecular-weight polyethylene [1][3][22] 43. Base description: Higher density than predecessor UltraDrive, absorbs more wax, faster and more durable [3][87] 44. Base graphic: Sublimation printed (heat and pressure embed ink into base material) [16] 45. Base colour note: Base colours are size dependent and cannot be swapped between sizes [1][22] 46. Die-cut base: Two base color variations per size to minimize waste [22] FLEX & RIDE 47. Flex rating: 5.5 out of 10 (medium) [1][6][22] 48. Flex feel: Medium — described as "playful yet responsive" [56][28] 49. Flex category per evo: Medium (evo standardizes 3-5 as medium) [21] 50. Flex description (reviewer): "a very lively flex that can bend easily but pop hard back into place" [19] 51. Torsional rigidity: Slightly more torsionally rigid than boards with similar flex ratings, due to carbon fiber [55] AVAILABLE SIZES (2027 model — Merchant verified) 52. Price comparison: "The Capita DOA costs -$4.05 less than the average snowboard price of $468.01" (boardoftheworld review for 2026) [36] 96. 2027 delivery timeline for Australia/NZ: April/May 2026 [39][104] 97. Previous year models available at discounts June-September; best deals around July 4th and Labor Day [72] RETAILERS & AVAILABILITY 98. Manufacturer direct: capitasnowboarding.com (US, CA, EU, JP) [22] 99. Retailer — evo.com (major US/global online retailer, reputable, price match guarantee) [101] 100. Retailer — The Ski Monster (US specialist shop, staff tests all gear sold) [6] 101. Retailer — Gorge Performance (US dealer) [3] 102. Retailer — Melbourne Snowboard Centre (Australia, carries 2027 preorder) [1][104] 103. Retailer — Auski Australia (2027 preorder) [108] 104. Retailer — Cardrona Corner (New Zealand, 2027 available) [107] 105. Retailer — Balmoral Boards (Australia, 2027 Super DOA preorder) [39] 106. Retailer — Amazon (US, limited previous year models available) [24] 107. Retailer — eBay (US, new and used available) [40] 108. Retailer — Milosport (US specialty shop) [25] 109. Retailer — SoCal Surf Shop (US) [41] 110. Retailer — Blauer Boardshop (US) [10] 111. Commonly sells out: "get it early in the season, it is pretty popular and sells out quite quickly" [61] WARRANTY 112. Warranty: 2 years from date of purchase, covering defects in material or workmanship [92][27] 113. Warranty excludes: Impact damage, rock/handrail damage, abuse, misuse, normal wear and tear [93] 114. Warranty claim process: Scan NFC chip to register board, then submit claim online [92][93] PERFORMANCE — REVIEW OPINIONS 115. Terrain: All-Mountain, Freestyle, Park (jumps emphasis), Carving on groomers [1][5][17] 116. Riding style: All-mountain freestyle — best for jumping, carving; weaker for jibbing and powder [5][17][19] 117. Ability level (manufacturer): Intermediate to advanced [5][36] 118. Ability level (reviewer consensus): Not for beginners; "even low intermediate riders would struggle with this" [13][36] 119. DISAGREEMENT — Beginner suitability: The Ski Monster says "any snowboarder, from beginners to seasoned riders, will feel comfortable on" it [6]. Multiple reviewers say it's NOT beginner friendly [5][13][36]. Reviewer consensus is more credible here. 120. Pop: Exceptional — "massive level of pop" and "springboard-like"; one of the board's greatest strengths [5][17][66] 121. Pop accessibility: "the most accessible pop of any board I've ridden… requires very little preload" [78] 122. Carving: Good but not elite — "carves pretty well, but it isn't a super carver" [19][66] 123. Edge hold: Good — solid on hardpack, "impressive for a freestyle board" [5][36][69] 124. Stability at speed: Good — "really stable at speeds" [13][78] 125. Dampness: Moderate — "a little more dampness than the Outsiders" but chatter in afternoon chop [66][78] 126. Butters/Presses: Harder than expected — "it will take more effort than you would think to get this board to flex longitudinally" [5][17] 127. Jibbing: Doable but "more for the advanced to expert jibber"; for easier jibbing, consider Capita Ultrafear or Pathfinder [5][17][66] 128. Powder performance: Weak point — "doesn't float that well" due to true twin centered stance; nose wants to dive in deep snow [5][17][19][63] 129. Switch riding: Excellent — true twin design provides equal performance in both directions [1][17] 130. Speed: Fast base — "super fast" sintered base, stable at high speeds [13] 131. Board of the World review ranking: 6th out of 38 in all-mountain category; 6th out of 36 in park category [36] 132. Snowboarding Profiles: DOA ranked 1st out of 16 in aggressive all-mountain-freestyle category (2017-18 review) [84] 133. Reviewer recommendation (Board of the World): "perfect board for intermediate to advanced level riders who want a board around the $500 price range" [36] AWARDS 134. Transworld Good Wood Awards: Won seven times in a row (unprecedented) [52][53][91] 135. Additional awards: Multiple Snowboarder Mag Most Wanted Awards [55] 136. CAPiTA's best-selling snowboard model [1][22] 137. Described as "one of the most popular freestyle boards of all time" [69] UPGRADE HISTORY 138. 2023 model year: Major upgrade — new P2 Superlight core (lighter, more pressable than Dual Blaster V2 core) [52][64] 139. 2025 model year: Hybrid HolySheet directly interwoven with carbon boosters (was separate before) [10][29][64] 140. 2025-2026 model year: No tech upgrades, graphic change only [17][64] 141. 2026-2027 model year: Expected to follow similar pattern — the DOA construction has been stable [17][52] COMPARABLE PRODUCTS / COMPETITORS 142. Competitor: CAPiTA Super DOA — upgraded version, lighter, faster HyperDrive base, 3D core, ~$120-200 more expensive; regular DOA "more than enough for 99% of riders" [7][35] 143. Competitor: YES. Greats (UnInc) — asymmetric sidecut, MidBite edge tech for better ice grip; slightly stiffer; "one all-mountain twin that actually rides well everywhere" [75][78] 144. Competitor: Jones Mountain Twin — directional twin, flex 7/10 (stiffer), better in powder, slightly more beginner-friendly, same price point; DOA better for freestyle/park [72][77] 145. Competitor: Never Summer Proto Type Two — rocker-camber-rocker profile, different feel; compared directly by The Good Ride [19] 146. Competitor: Ride Shadowban — directional option, recommended as alternative for all-mountain use [80] 147. Competitor: Bataleon Evil Twin Plus — similar spec but with lifted contact points (Triple Base Technology) making it easier to ride for beginners [17] 148. Competitor: CAPiTA Outerspace Living — softer, cheaper ($529.95), better in trees/powder, less aggressive carving [67] 149. Competitor: CAPiTA Mercury — more versatile/directional variant, larger rocker sections, better for varied conditions [76] 150. In-line comparison: DOA is more freestyle-oriented; Mercury/Mountain Twin more all-mountain versatile [72][77] 151. DOA vs Jones Mountain Twin warranty: Jones offers one year longer warranty [72] USER EXPERIENCE — FORUM OPINIONS 152. Forum opinion (SnowboardingForum.com): "one of the most popular freestyle boards of all time… how easy it is to access" [69] 153. Forum: "Carves very nicely for a twin, very agile sidecut, the pop is plentiful and effortless" [69] 154. Forum: "honestly cant think of a more perfect twin for riding the entire mountain, assuming there isnt a foot or more of fresh snow" [69] 155. Forum concern (edge hold on ice): "DOA: good enough in hard snow for northeast?" — mixed opinions, Yes boards noted for better ice grip [80][74] 156. Forum: DOA can feel "catchy" especially for riders coming from rocker boards [5][7] 157. Forum: DOA vs YES Greats debate — "Really not worth thinking about any of the tiny differences other than" asymmetric sidecut [75] 158. Reviewer concern: "It didn't realize how stiff it would be or that it would take some getting used to" when coming from rocker boards [5] 159. Board of the World: Reviewer spent 250+ days on DOA across multiple seasons — "sheer perfection" once adjusted [52][64] DESIGN & AESTHETICS 160. Graphic style: Distinctive female character on topsheet with various names over the years (Acid Mother Guru, Queen of Eternity, Goddess of Eternal Sleep, Witch of the Woods, Lady Death) [52] 161. Graphic controversy: Some riders have avoided the board due to graphic content; past versions featured "bikini-clad girls" and similar imagery [86] 162. Graphics are size-dependent: Different graphic per length size [1][22] SUSTAINABILITY & CERTIFICATIONS 163. Certified B Corp [44] 164. Energy Globe Award for Austria (2017) — "known as Nature's Nobel Prize" [47] 165. Water-based UV curable solventless inks in printing [22][24] 166. Zero toxic lacquer in topsheet (PLT technology) [22][24] 167. 100% recyclable shrink wrap on finished boards [43] 168. Plant-based bio resins (Magic Bean) with FSC certified wood cores [43] 169. Recycling: All production scraps recycled including base materials, tip/tail trimmings, sidewall ABS, protection film, wood core waste [43] ADDITIONAL ATTRIBUTES 170. Binding compatibility: All standard 2x4 insert pattern bindings [1] 171. Recommended binding pairings (reviewer): Union Force, Union Falcor [62][82] 172. Boot size guidelines: Standard widths for up to size 10; wides for 10-12 [19]
